reasons: New signal: `exofop_tois`, `exofop_ctois` and `published_signal` are all empty, and the record shows no TOI, CTOI, TCE or TESS EB match in the catalogues of 2026-10-15; `ephemeris_match_likely_sources` and `ephemeris_match_contaminated_stars` are empty.

Strong, repeatable detection: `MES` 38.9 in S98, S32 TESS-SPOC recovered at SNR 45.9 against expected 35.9 (`other_sector_results`), `joint_search_snr` 62.5 against `joint_search_highest_null_snr` 16.7, `joint_search_detected` True, `period_pile_up_ratio` 0.2. The folded S98 and S32 panels of the all-sector figure show a clean flat-bottomed transit with ingress and egress in both sectors.

Dip is on the target: `pixel_verdict` on target in both sectors (`pixel_verdicts_by_sector` S32 SNR 10.9, S98 SNR 7.7, best star TIC 264626874); both difference images peak on the target pixel with the free-fit cross on the target. The 'neighbour able to cause dip' caution (`gaia_neighbours_able_to_cause_dip`: two G~15.5 stars at 27" and 57" needing 24-27% eclipses) is answered by this and by TRICERATOPS `nfpp_mean` 0 with `nearby_scenarios_excluded` True.

Transit shape is consistent with a companion of the target star: `stellar_density_fit_to_tic_ratio` 0.966, `fitted_to_expected_scaled_semi_major_axis` 1.11, `transit_grazing` False with `fit_impact_parameter` 0.745 +/- 0.0326, `odd_even_difference_sigma` 1.30, `secondary_depth_ppm` -18 +/- 34 (no secondary eclipse; `secondary_maximum_planet_depth_ppm` 157). The secondary panel of the figure shows nothing at phase 0.5.

Radius is below the stellar threshold: `planet_radius_earth_radii` 17.68 +/- 0.88 (about 1.6 Jupiter radii) from `fit_radius_ratio` 0.0560 on a `stellar_radius_solar_radii` 2.89514 host that LAMOST classes A1V (`lamost_spectra`). An inflated giant planet of this size around a hot A star is plausible; the radius is not grazing-degenerate.

The 'ellipsoidal variation detected' caution is the only reason for the mechanical hold, and I weigh it as a caveat rather than a disqualifier: `ellipsoidal_amplitude_ppm_by_sector` is S32 163 +/- 45 (3.6 sigma, 600 s SPOC data) and S98 155 +/- 348 (uninformative), so it rests on one sector. The host has `gaia_vbroad_km_s` 185, a rapidly rotating A star where residual pulsation or rotational variability at half the orbital period can mimic an ellipsoidal term. The implied `ellipsoidal_companion_mass_solar_masses` 0.105 is not excluded by Gaia RV (`gaia_rv_companion_mass_upper_limit_solar_masses` 0.264, `gaia_rv_variable` False), but neither is it confirmed, so the evidence does not show the companion is most likely stellar.

Why not 'held': `released_tess_sectors_not_in_all_sector_verification` is empty, so no further data in hand can decide the ellipsoidal question; what decides it is radial-velocity follow-up of this Tmag 10.07 star, which is exactly what a CTOI listing prompts. The ellipsoidal amplitude and implied mass should be written into the CTOI comment.

TRICERATOPS supports a planet on target: `most_likely_scenario` TP on TIC 264626874, `fpp_mean` 0.07462 +/- 0.082 ('likely planet'; an earlier run in the record gave 0.01475). It is not statistically validated, which is consistent with proposing a candidate rather than a confirmed planet.

The large pipeline-level sector depth difference (`depth_ppm_by_sector` S98 2770 +/- 57 versus S32 3385 +/- 45, `sector_depth_consistency_p_value` 2.64e-17) is attributable to the different QLP and SPOC processing rather than to the star, because the uniform cutout apertures agree across sectors (`cutout_sector_depth_consistency_p_value` 0.699, all apertures 2694-3096 ppm). This should be noted, not treated as a red flag.

Gaia shows no sign of a bright stellar companion: `gaia_ruwe` 1.19, `gaia_non_single_star` 0, `gaia_eclipsing_binary` False, `vsx_binaries` empty. The second LAMOST spectrum (A2V at 4.6 arcsec, RV -20 versus -14 km/s, 'no Gaia source in the fibre') is most simply the same rapidly rotating star in an offset fibre, and a 6 km/s shift is not significant for a star with `gaia_vbroad_km_s` 185.
